A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChatInject work. All 28 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G, were readable and could be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original ChatInject evaluations on InjecAgent and AgentDojo, including attack success and utility results in Tables 1–2 and additional experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark evaluations and supplementary experiments, including the results in Tables 1–2 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The template-formatting method, simulated multi-turn dialogues, reasoning and tool-calling hooks, and mixture-of-templates procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the same InjecAgent scenarios, AgentDojo domains, and adapted human jailbreak dialogues evaluated in Appendix C.1. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including Default InjecPrompt, Default Multi-turn, the adapted real-attack comparison, and the detector and prompt-based defenses.

E3.justification: The model configurations, ASR and utility metrics, decoding settings, sample counts, and testing procedures in Section 3.3 and the appendices are identical.

E4.justification: The turn-count, persuasion, attention, homoglyph, template-mixing, and perturbation analyses are retained without changes to their questions or evidence.

E5.justification: Both report the same five-seed experiments, mean and standard-deviation displays, and 95% Wilson confidence intervals, including Appendix E.

E6.justification: All numerical result entries and qualitative findings match across the main text and appendices. The small Table 5 heading adjustment changes no values.

T1.justification: The threat-model assumptions and payload definitions in Section 3, attention calculation in Appendix C.3, and embedding-similarity definitions in Appendix D.3 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about attack effectiveness, cross-model transferability, and weaknesses of existing defenses.

C2.justification: Interpretations of template authority, transferability, and utility degradation are identical. Appendix B retains the same limitations concerning synthetic dialogues, internal analysis, and defenses.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the direct GitHub repository link with a GitHub Pages project-page link, changing the documented access route. Implementation details are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the hosted resources differ.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to earlier prompt-injection, template-abuse, and multi-turn attack research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 30 January 2026 to v3 dated 13 April 2026, and the access-link text changes. The manuscript prose and section structure otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: Table 5 slightly shifts the horizontal position of its User column heading. Apart from the first-page link and version stamp, the remaining figures, tables, captions, and page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, and appendices are unchanged. The revised access link and tiny Table 5 alignment adjustment produce no meaningful demonstrated quality gain or loss; the PDFs provide no evidence that the new link improves access to research materials.
